b:
Among the silver wires
a few black threads
peep through

The wrinkles of age, and with them
the weariness of the old

In her clothes
so many tears
and nothing obscene in them

Worn-out rubber slippers
and a pushcart as her chariot,
like siblings born with her

The cawing of black crows
greets her like a temple bell

Up before us and asleep after us,
she
is the representative
of those our progressive society
has pushed behind

You people of foolish custom
who turn your face away
when she appears in front of you:

she
is the power of cleanliness
in this world that wanders in its dirt!
note: She is a street sweeper. Some people still consider it a bad omen to see a sweeper first thing in the morning; the poem answers that superstition.
